title_en: Liu Lei v. Wang Weijian, Zhu Kairong, and Tianan Insurance Yancheng Central Sub-branch — dispute over compensation for personal injury in a traffic accident
ruling_gist_en: Where a policyholder purchases motor vehicle third-party liability insurance through a marketing department established by an insurance company, and a marketing staff member of the department, for the purpose of embezzling the premium, fills in a fake insurance policy that is identical in content and form to a genuine policy, affixes a forged insurance company business seal, and sells and delivers it to the policyholder through a salesperson within the marketing department, the policyholder, as an innocent and bona fide purchaser, has reason to believe that the insurance purchased is genuine, and the content of the policy does not violate relevant legal provisions. In civil law, the conduct of the marketing department shall be deemed as that of the insurance company. Therefore, even though the insurance policy held by the policyholder is fake, the insurance company cannot be exempted from the civil liability it shall bear under the insurance contract according to law.

full_text_en:
Liu Lei v. Wang Weijian, Zhu Kairong, and Tianan Insurance Yancheng Central Sub-branch — Dispute over Compensation for Personal Injury in a Traffic Accident

Ruling Summary

Where an insurance applicant purchases motor vehicle third-party liability insurance through a sales department established by the insurance company, and a salesperson of that department, for the purpose of embezzling the insurance premium, fills in a forged policy that is identical in content and form to a genuine policy, affixes a forged insurance company business seal, and sells and delivers it to the applicant through a salesperson within that same sales department, the bona fide applicant, who is unaware of the forgery, has reason to believe that the insurance purchased is genuine, and the content of the policy does not violate relevant legal provisions. The conduct of the sales department shall, in civil law, be deemed the conduct of the insurance company. Therefore, even though the policy held by the applicant is forged, this does not exempt the insurance company from the civil liability it should bear under the insurance contract in accordance with the law.

Plaintiff: Liu Lei, male, 22 years old, residing at the dormitory of Changshu Yinghuan Weaving, Printing and Dyeing Co., Ltd.

Defendants:
*   Wang Weijian, male, 36 years old, residing in Zhupu Village, Xiaojian Town, Xiangshui County, Jiangsu Province.
*   Zhu Kairong, male, 40 years old, residing in Tuqiao Village, Xiaojian Town, Xiangshui County, Jiangsu Province.
*   Tianan Insurance Co., Ltd. Yancheng Central Sub-branch, domiciled at Jiefang South Road, Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.
    Person in Charge: Yu Zhengxiang, General Manager of the company.

The plaintiff, Liu Lei, initiated civil proceedings with the Changshu People's Court against the defendants Wang Weijian, Zhu Kairong, and Tianan Insurance Co., Ltd. Yancheng Central Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch) regarding a dispute over compensation for personal injury in a road traffic accident.

Plaintiff's Allegations: At approximately 10:00 p.m. on July 20, 2005, while the defendant Wang Weijian was turning the defendant Zhu Kairong's tricycle motorcycle (license plate Su JFR978) on the village road near Wuzhuang Village, Miaonan Village, it collided with the electric bicycle ridden by the plaintiff, causing the plaintiff to be injured. The Traffic Police Brigade determined that Wang Weijian bore primary responsibility for the accident and Liu Lei bore secondary responsibility. The plaintiff requested the court to order the defendants to compensate for medical expenses, lost wages, nursing fees, transportation fees, hospitalization meal subsidies, and ambulance fees, totaling RMB 24,172. Disability-related costs were to be claimed after assessment. During the proceedings, the plaintiff amended the relevant claims, requesting the defendants to compensate for medical expenses of RMB 27,516, ambulance fees of RMB 40, lost wages of RMB 35,850, nursing fees of RMB 7,625, transportation fees of RMB 1,076, hospitalization meal subsidies of RMB 1,125, nutrition expenses of RMB 3,050, disability compensation of RMB 28,168, moral damages of RMB 5,000, meal expenses of RMB 325, and dining expenses of RMB 3,100, totaling RMB 112,875.

The defendants Wang Weijian and Zhu Kairong did not submit a defense.

Defendant's Defense (Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch): After receiving from the court the plaintiff Liu Lei's complaint and attached documents, our company verified that we had never issued the motorcycle insurance policy document to the defendant Zhu Kairong. We discovered that the business seal on the policy document is inconsistent with our company's seal. No insurance contract relationship has ever been formed between our company and Zhu Kairong regarding the motorcycle insurance. Therefore, our company should not bear compensation liability for the forged policy in this traffic accident compensation case. We request that the court dismiss the plaintiff's claims against our company.

Basic Facts Found by the Court of First Instance (Changshu People's Court):

At approximately 10:00 p.m. on July 20, 2005, while the defendant Wang Weijian was turning the "New Feeling" brand three-wheeled cargo motorcycle (license plate Su JFR978) on the village road near Wuzhuang Village, Miaonan Village, the left side of the front wheel and other parts collided with the right side bumper and other parts of an unlicensed "Aiqike" brand electric bicycle ridden by the plaintiff Liu Lei, who was traveling from south to north, causing Liu Lei to be injured and the electric bicycle to be damaged. After the incident, the Changshu Public Security Bureau Traffic Patrol Police Brigade conducted an investigation and, on August 1, 2005, issued Traffic Accident Determination No. 2005-07126. It determined that Wang Weijian, driving at night and turning on the road, failed to ensure he did not impede the passage of other vehicles, which was the primary cause of the accident. His conduct violated Article 49, Paragraph 2 of the *Regulations for the Implementation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Road Traffic Safety* and Article 38, Item (1) of the *Jiangsu Province Road Traffic Safety Regulations*. Liu Lei, riding an unlicensed electric bicycle at night without its lights on and with brakes that were later tested and found to be substandard, and at a relatively high speed, was also a contributing cause of the accident. His conduct violated Article 18, Paragraph 3, Article 38 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on Road Traffic Safety* and Article 16, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the *Jiangsu Province Road Traffic Safety Regulations*. The determination held Wang Weijian primarily responsible and Liu Lei secondarily responsible for the accident.

After being injured, the plaintiff Liu Lei was rescued and taken to Changshu New District Hospital for treatment, diagnosed with an open fracture of the left tibia and fibula, and hospitalized for 12 days. Subsequently, Liu Lei was hospitalized at Changshu Second People's Hospital for 22 days. From August 15 to 19, 2006, Liu Lei was again hospitalized at Changshu Second People's Hospital for 4 days. From November 17 to December 1, 2006, Liu Lei was hospitalized at the Sixth People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai Jiao Tong University for 13.5 days. From December 1 to 12, 2006, Liu Lei continued hospitalization at Wanping Area Hospital, Xuhui District, Shanghai for 11 days. Additionally, Liu Lei received outpatient treatment at the above hospitals and Changshu Meili Central Health Center after the injury. Liu Lei incurred medical expenses totaling RMB 27,556.70. After the injury, Liu Lei was cared for by relatives. During the proceedings, upon Liu Lei's application, the Changshu People's Court commissioned the Judicial Appraisal Institute of Changshu First People's Hospital to appraise Liu Lei's disability grade, period of lost wages, period and number of nursing persons, and period for nutritional support. On July 9, 2007, the institute issued an appraisal conclusion, stating that Liu Lei's open fracture of the left tibia and fibula resulting from the traffic accident constituted a Grade 10 disability; the period of lost wages was from the injury until the day before the appraisal; one person was required for nursing, and nutritional support was needed during hospitalization and for 90 days after discharge.

Separately, it was found: The plaintiff Liu Lei worked at Changshu Yinghuan Weaving, Printing and Dyeing Co., Ltd., claiming a daily income of RMB 50. The registered owner of the "New Feeling" three-wheeled cargo motorcycle (license plate Su JFR978) driven by defendant Wang Weijian was defendant Zhu Kairong. After the accident, Wang Weijian provided the Changshu Public Security Bureau Traffic Patrol Police Brigade with an insurance policy (No. 0500064813) for the Su JFR978 "New Feeling" three-wheeled cargo motorcycle. The policy indicated that the motorcycle was insured with Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch for a third-party comprehensive damage liability with a liability limit of RMB 20,000, effective from 00:00 on May 30, 2005 to 24:00 on May 29, 2006. During the proceedings, the Changshu People's Court commissioned the Yancheng Public Security Bureau to assist in investigating the insurance policy (No. 0500064813) for the Su JFR978 three-wheeled cargo motorcycle. The investigation verified that this policy was one of the forged policies produced by Liu Mingxing, a staff member of the sales department.

It was further found: Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch had a sales department in Xiangshui. This sales department used the business seal of Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch when entering into insurance contracts externally. Liu Mingxing previously served as the head of this sales department. During his tenure, Liu Mingxing forged the business seal of Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch, privately printed insurance policies, and sold them. In this case, the insurance policy (No. 0500064813) for the Su JFR978 three-wheeled cargo motorcycle was sold by Liu Mingxing through a salesperson at the Xiangshui sales department, and the content was filled in by the salesperson. On September 7, 2005, Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch filed a report with the Yancheng Public Security Bureau, stating that since December 2004, Liu Mingxing had privately engraved the company's official seal, privately printed policies, and defrauded multiple persons of insurance premiums. On September 30, 2005, the Yancheng Public Security Bureau decided to file a case for investigation. On October 20, 2005, Liu Mingxing was criminally detained by the Yancheng Public Security Bureau on suspicion of embezzlement. On November 25, 2005, the Yancheng People's Procuratorate approved the arrest of Liu Mingxing on suspicion of contract fraud. Liu Mingxing has now been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment by the Xiangshui People's Court for the crime of contract fraud.

Issue in Dispute at First Instance: Whether the defendant Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch should bear insurance compensation liability.

Opinion of the Court (First Instance, Changshu People's Court):

The plaintiff Liu Lei filed the lawsuit regarding the losses caused by this accident with the court before April 1, 2006. According to the regulations in effect before July 1, 2006, where a motor vehicle traffic accident causes personal injury or property loss, the insurance company shall compensate for the losses arising from the accident within the insurance liability limit for third-party liability insurance. The compensation liability borne by the insurance company within the insurance liability limit for third-party liability insurance is a no-fault liability. The insurance company shall compensate regardless of whether the parties involved in the traffic accident were at fault. For losses exceeding the insurance liability limit, if the accident occurs between a motor vehicle and a non-motor vehicle driver or pedestrian, the motor vehicle party shall bear liability. However, if there is evidence proving that the non-motor vehicle driver or pedestrian violated road traffic safety laws or regulations and that the motor vehicle driver has taken necessary measures, the liability of the motor vehicle party shall be reduced.

The insurance policy (No. 0500064813) for the "New Feeling" three-wheeled cargo motorcycle (license plate Su JFR978) provided by the defendant Wang Weijian to the traffic police department after the accident is indeed a forged policy. However, this was caused by the criminal conduct of Liu Mingxing. At the time Liu Mingxing committed the crime using the forged policy, he was the head of the sales department established by Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch in Xiangshui. The forged policy was sold through the sales outlet of the sales department. This shows that Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch failed in its management of the Xiangshui sales department and was clearly at fault in the process of the Xiangshui sales department selling the forged policies produced by Liu Mingxing. Therefore, Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch should bear responsibility for this.

The Traffic Police Brigade's determination that the defendant Wang Weijian bore primary responsibility and the plaintiff Liu Lei bore secondary responsibility for this accident was proper and is adopted. The defendants Wang Weijian and Zhu Kairong are the driver and registered owner, respectively, of the Su JFR978 "New Feeling" three-wheeled cargo motorcycle. As both failed to appear in court, the court could not ascertain whether there were grounds for their exemption from liability. Consequently, they shall jointly bear compensation liability for the losses caused to Liu Lei in the accident. Given that Liu Lei was also at fault for the accident and bore secondary responsibility, the compensation liability of Wang Weijian and Zhu Kairong shall be correspondingly reduced. Wang Weijian and Zhu Kairong shall bear 80% of the compensation liability for Liu Lei's losses caused by the accident.

As for the losses incurred by the plaintiff Liu Lei in the accident and the compensation expenses he claimed, they shall be calculated according to the scope, items, and standards stipulated in the Supreme People's Court's *Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Personal Injury*.

Regarding medical expenses: determined as RMB 27,556.
Regarding lost wages: determined as RMB 26,937.69.
Regarding nursing fees: determined as RMB 6,100.
Regarding transportation fees: discretionarily determined as RMB 800.
Regarding hospitalization meal subsidies: determined as RMB 1,125.
Regarding nutrition expenses: determined as RMB 1,525.
Regarding disability compensation: determined as RMB 28,168.
Regarding moral damages: determined as RMB 5,000.
Regarding the meal expenses and dining expenses claimed by the plaintiff Liu Lei: these are not within the scope or items of compensation provided by law, and are not supported.

In summary, the losses of the plaintiff Liu Lei caused by this accident, including medical expenses of RMB 27,556, lost wages of RMB 26,937.69, nursing fees of RMB 6,100, transportation fees of RMB 800, hospitalization meal subsidies of RMB 1,125, nutrition expenses of RMB 1,525, disability compensation of RMB 28,168, and moral damages of RMB 5,000, total RMB 97,211.69. Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch shall compensate Liu Lei within the liability limit of the third-party liability insurance in the amount of RMB 20,000. For the amount exceeding the liability limit, which is RMB 77,211.69, the defendants Wang Weijian and Zhu Kairong shall compensate Liu Lei at a ratio of 80%, amounting to RMB 61,769.35. Wang Weijian and Zhu Kairong, having been lawfully summoned by the court, failed to appear without justifiable reasons. This shall be deemed as their waiver of the right to appear and defend, and any adverse consequences possibly arising therefrom shall be borne by themselves.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 130 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, Paragraph 1 of Article 76 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on Road Traffic Safety*, Articles 1, 2, 17, and 18 of the Supreme People's Court's *Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Personal Injury*, and Articles 1, Paragraph 2 of Article 8, Articles 10 and 11 of the Supreme People's Court's *Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Determination of Liability for Compensation for Mental Damage in Civil Torts*, the Changshu People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 17, 2007:

1.  The defendant Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch shall compensate the plaintiff Liu Lei for medical expenses, lost wages, nursing fees, transportation fees, hospitalization meal subsidies, nutrition expenses, disability compensation, and moral damages arising from the traffic accident, totaling RMB 20,000. This shall be performed within ten days after this judgment takes effect.
2.  The defendants Wang Weijian and Zhu Kairong shall compensate the plaintiff Liu Lei for medical expenses, lost wages, nursing fees, transportation fees, hospitalization meal subsidies, nutrition expenses, disability compensation, and moral damages arising from the traffic accident, totaling RMB 61,769.35. This shall be performed within ten days after this judgment takes effect.
3.  The remaining claims of the plaintiff Liu Lei are dismissed.

Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch, dissatisfied with the first-instance civil judgment, appealed to the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, stating:
(1) The first-instance court's reliance solely on a forged policy and the criminal's confession in the public security department to conclude that the insurance company failed in management and thereby should bear liability is unfounded in law.
(2) The criminal Liu Mingxing was originally the head of our company's Xiangshui sales department. However, Liu Mingxing left the company without authorization in December 2004 and was no longer the head of the insurance company's Xiangshui sales department from 2005 onwards. His criminal conduct is unrelated to the insurance company's management and training, and the insurance company should not bear civil compensation liability.
(3) This case was converted from a summary procedure to an ordinary procedure in October 2007. However, during the trial on October 22, 2007, people's jurors Ji Baoqi and Zhang Liyun were not present, and the case was still tried solely by Shao Jun. The procedure was illegal, rendering the result invalid. We request the appellate court to amend the judgment according to law.
The appellees Liu Lei, Wang Weijian, and Zhu Kairong did not submit a defense.

The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, upon second instance, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Another fact was found in the second instance: On October 22, 2007, at 8:30 a.m., the second trial session of this case was conducted in the Fourth Courtroom of the Changshu People's Court. People's jurors Ji Baoqi and Zhang Liyun were both present at the trial and signed the trial record.

Issue in Dispute at Second Instance: The same as the first instance: Whether the appellant Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch should bear insurance compensation liability.

Opinion of the Court (Second Instance, Suzhou Intermediate People's Court):

The appellant Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch had a sales department in Xiangshui. This sales department used the business seal of Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch when entering into insurance contracts externally. Liu Mingxing admitted to previously serving as the head of this sales department and, during his tenure, forged the business seal of Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch, privately printed insurance policies, and sold them. The appellant claims that Liu Mingxing left the company without authorization in December 2004 and was no longer the head of the appellant's Xiangshui sales department from 2005 onwards, but failed to provide evidence to support this claim. Moreover, in this case, the insurance policy (No. 0500064813) for the Su JFR978 three-wheeled cargo motorcycle was sold by Liu Mingxing through a salesperson at the Xiangshui sales department. The content was filled in by the salesperson, and the content and form of the policy were consistent with a genuine policy. The insured, the defendant at first instance Zhu Kairong, as a bona fide counterparty, purchased the third-party comprehensive damage liability insurance at the appellant's Xiangshui sales department. Zhu Kairong had reason to believe that the insurance he purchased was genuine, and the content of the policy did not violate relevant legal provisions. The conduct of the Xiangshui sales department shall, in civil law, be deemed the conduct of the appellant. Therefore, although the policy held by Zhu Kairong was forged, this was caused by the appellant's employee acting within the scope of his duties, and Zhu Kairong had no means of detecting it. The appellant should have strengthened its management and supervision. Consequently, the appellant cannot be exempted from the civil liability it should bear. The Changshu People's Court's decision that the appellant bear compensation liability within its insurance limit was not improper.

Regarding the appellant Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch's procedural appeal ground that the first-instance trial procedure was illegal, as it is inconsistent with the facts, it is not supported.

In summary, none of the appellant Tianan Yancheng Sub-branch's grounds for appeal are sustainable. The judgment of the court of first instance was proper and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Item (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on June 19, 2008:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
